description.narrative: Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term awards administered by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. They aim to contribute to the development needs of Australia's partner countries in line with bilateral and regional agreements. They provide opportunities for people from developing countries, particularly those countries located in the Indo-Pacific region, to undertake full time undergraduate or postgraduate study at participating Australian universities and Technical and Further Education (TAFE) institutions. The study and research opportunities provided by Australia Awards Scholarships develop the skills and knowledge of individuals to drive change and contribute to development in their own countries.

description.narrative: Dr Thomas Wangi, an Australia Awards alumni earned his Doctoral Degree in Philosophy at the Australian National University (ANU). Since returning to Papua New Guinea (PNG), Dr Wangi has continued his work as a Senior Research Fellow at the PNG National Research Institute and Research Associate with the Centre for Applied Macroeconomic Analysis and Development Policy Centre at the ANU. Dr Wangi is driving important research connections between PNG and Australia, collaborating closely with ANU’s Professor Stephen Howes and the Lowy Institute of Public Policy. As lead researcher on monetary policy in PNG, Dr Wangi’s influential work includes a key policy paper titled “Impact of Excess Reserves on Monetary Policy Transmission in Papua New Guinea (CAMA Working Paper 16/2024, Crawford School of Public Policy, ANU). The paper presents important conclusions on monetary policy and financial stability in PNG.

In 2024, Australia Awards Timor-Leste launched a pilot initiative to help people with disability overcome a key barrier to accessing the scholarship program: English language proficiency. Through a merit-based process, five aspiring scholars—80% of whom were women—were selected for an English language short course at the University of Adelaide English Language Centre. ‍ Over 11 weeks, participants received intensive English instruction, lived with Australian host families, and gained first-hand experience of life in Australia as people with disability. The course not only accelerated participants’ language acquisition, but also boosted their independence and confidence to study at an Australian university in the future. ‍ Following the program, all participants reported significant improvement in their English reading, writing, listening, and speaking. Two raised their IELTS scores by a full band. Importantly, all five have since applied for the next Australia Awards Scholarship intake and are actively engaged in additional professional development opportunities using their improved English skills. ‍ This pilot is a powerful example of how targeted support can help reduce barriers and unlock potential—advancing equity, inclusion, and opportunity for Timorese people with disability.
